name: Albumin

usual_adult_dose.dose: 50–75 g/day IV; rate not exceeding 2 mL/min in hypoproteinemic patients. Individualize to indication/response [[ALBPI]]

monitoring: Monitor hemodynamic response and overload; renal insufficiency, heart failure and stable chronic anemia increase overload risk [[ALBPI]]

key_interactions.effect: Dilution can cause severe hemolysis/acute renal failure [[ALBPI]]
key_interactions.action: Do not use alone as diluent; acceptable diluents include 0.9% saline or 5% dextrose [[ALBPI]]

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Protein hydrolysates, amino-acid or alcohol-containing solutions

evidence.title: Concentration and dialysis evidence
evidence.intro: This summary is specific to a 25% US product; concentration and local insert matter.

rows.findings: 5% albumin is preferred for usual volume deficits; 25% provides greater oncotic activity. Albumin is not protein nutrition or a regular dialysis regimen.
rows.limitations: No blanket benefit inferred for low serum albumin or chronic nephrotic edema.

rows.design: Randomized crossover; 65 hospitalized AKI/ESKD patients, albumin<3 g/dL; 249 sessions.
rows.intervention: 100 mL 25% albumin versus 100 mL 0.9% saline at dialysis initiation; study protocol.
rows.findings: KDOQI-defined hypotension 15% with saline versus 7% with albumin(P=0.002); lowest systolic pressure 83 versus 90 mmHg(P=0.035).
rows.limitations: Selected hypoalbuminemic inpatients, short-term session outcomes. Does not establish routine outpatient benefit, mortality benefit or a universal dialysis prescription.
